The test is satisfactory only if all the conditions of paragraphs 5.2.1 to 5.2.7 are satisfied at the same time.

requirements.text: In the frontal impact test, the head performance criterion (HPC) of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy in the driver's seat shall not exceed 1000.

In the frontal impact test, the resultant head acceleration of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively and excluding rebound movement of the head.
In the frontal impact test, the axial tensile neck force of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 3.3 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 3.1 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the neck bending moment about the y axis of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
In the frontal impact test, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 42 mm.
In the frontal impact test, the viscous criterion (V*C) for the thorax of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 1.0 m/s.
In the frontal impact test, the femur force criterion (FFC) of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 9.07 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the head performance criterion (HPC) of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy in the outboard passenger seat shall not exceed 1000.

In the frontal impact test, the resultant head acceleration of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively and excluding rebound movement of the head.
In the frontal impact test, the axial tensile neck force of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 2.9 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 2.7 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the neck bending moment about the y axis of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
In the frontal impact test of an M1 vehicle, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 34 mm.
In the frontal impact test, the viscous criterion (V*C) for the thorax of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 1.0 m/s.
In the frontal impact test, the femur force criterion (FFC) of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 7 kN.

After the frontal impact test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 80 mm in the upwards vertical direction. Vehicles meeting the steering wheel displacement requirements of either Regulation No. 12 or No. 94 are deemed to comply.

After the frontal impact test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 100 mm in the rearward horizontal direction. Vehicles meeting the steering wheel displacement requirements of either Regulation No. 12 or No. 94 are deemed to comply.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage: after the frontal impact test, the high voltage buses, including the coupling system for charging the REESS and the vehicle inlet in the bumper, shall meet at least one of the four criteria of paragraphs 5.2.8.1.1 to 5.2.8.1.4.2. If an automatic disconnect function or devices that divide the electric power train circuit are fitted, this applies to each disconnected or divided circuit after activation. The isolation resistance criterion (5.2.8.1.4) shall not apply if more than a single potential of a part of the high voltage bus is not protected to IPXXB.

requirements.text: In the frontal impact test, the vehicle (fitted with the front bumper module) shall impact the barrier at a speed of 50 -0/+1 km/h; however, if the test was performed at a higher impact speed and the vehicle met the requirements, the test shall be considered satisfactory.

The frontal impact shall be made against a barrier consisting of a reinforced concrete block not less than 3 m wide in front, not less than 1.5 m high and weighing at least 70 metric tons, with a flat, vertical front face perpendicular to the axis of the run-up track covered with plywood boards 20 ± 2 mm thick in good condition (a structure on a steel plate at least 25 mm thick may be placed between the plywood and the barrier; a barrier with different characteristics may be used provided its impact surface area is greater than the frontal crash area of the vehicle and it gives equivalent results).

The vehicle shall reach the barrier on a course perpendicular to the collision wall, with a maximum lateral misalignment of ± 30 cm between the vertical median line of the front of the vehicle and the vertical median line of the collision wall.

The test vehicle shall be representative of the series production, shall include all the equipment normally fitted (including the front bumper module as produced) and shall be in normal running order; some components may be replaced by equivalent masses where this substitution clearly has no noticeable effect on the results measured.

requirements.text: For the frontal impact test, the mass of the vehicle submitted shall be the unladen kerb mass.

For vehicles with a high voltage electric power train (EV/PHEV variant with charging inlet in the bumper), the electric power train shall be energized during the test with or without the operation of the original electrical energy sources; by agreement between Technical Service and manufacturer, the test may be performed with all or parts of the electric power train not energized insofar as there is no negative influence on the test result, in which case for the parts not energized the protection against electrical shock shall be proved by either physical protection or isolation resistance and appropriate additional evidence.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage, then after the vehicle impact test the physical protection of its high voltage live parts shall meet paragraph 5.2.8.1.3. The physical protection is made up of the surrounding parts that remain after all parts that can be opened, disassembled or removed without tools have been opened or removed. To pass, the jointed test finger (Figure 3), inserted into any gap or opening with a test force of 10 N ± 10 per cent and articulated through every position up to 90 degrees at both joints, shall be unable to contact high voltage live parts.

requirements.text: If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and post-crash electrical safety is demonstrated by voltage measurement, the high voltage bus voltages (Ub, U1, U2) shall be measured not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact. This does not apply if the test is performed with the electric power train not energized.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and post-crash electrical safety is demonstrated by low electrical energy, the Total Energy (TE) shall be determined from measurements taken not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact. TE is either the integral of Ub x Ie from closing of switch S1 until Ub falls below 60 V DC, or TE = 0.5 x Cx x Ub² for X-capacitors, or TEy1 = 0.5 x Cy1 x U1² and TEy2 = 0.5 x Cy2 x U2² for Y-capacitors. This does not apply if the test is performed with the electric power train not energized.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and post-crash electrical safety is demonstrated by isolation resistance, the isolation resistance of each high voltage bus (measured separately for each conductively isolated circuit) shall be determined from measurements made a minimum of 10 seconds after the impact. Any modifications made for the measurement shall not influence the test results.
